name: Oak Tree
overview: The oak tree in Scripture symbolizes strength, endurance, and significant historical moments. It served as a physical landmark, as seen when Jacob hid idols beneath an oak near Shechem (Genesis 35:4) and Deborah was buried under an oak called Allonbachuth, the oak of weeping (Genesis 35:8). The oak's sturdy branches played a pivotal role in the tragic death of Absalom, who became entangled in its boughs during his rebellion against King David (2 Samuel 18:9,14). Additionally, oaks from Bashan were valued for their strong wood, used to craft oars (Ezekiel 27:6), while the oak's strength is likened to the might of the Amorite people whom God destroyed (Amos 2:9). These references highlight the oak as a symbol of both natural strength and significant divine encounters in biblical history.
